title: Jesse Marcel says weather balloon was a cover story

tellings.quote: Cut to 1978. Lieutenant Colonel Jesse Marcel said that this was all just a cover story
he said when you know, they came to take pictures or the pictures they took he said that wasn't the stuff that we found.
tellings.difference: Says specifically that the debris in the press photographs was not the material Marcel found.
tellings.link_reason: In both, Jesse Marcel says the debris shown publicly was a cover for what was really found at Roswell.

plain: Jesse Marcel Sr., an Air Force officer at Roswell, New Mexico, when debris was found there in 1947, is said to have come forward in 1978 and called the military's weather-balloon explanation a cover story. Michels tells it himself, saying Lieutenant Colonel Marcel claimed he was "forced to do this photo op" with a weather balloon. In another episode Michels dates this to 1979 and adds that Marcel said he handled "memory metal," metal that springs back into shape. A guest named Bob Lazar, who mentions the general Roger Ramey, says Marcel claimed the debris in the press photographs "wasn't the stuff that we found." If true, it would mean the real Roswell material was swapped out and hidden.
